record.notes: The per-host ceiling is the one a single large release meets. The API documentation is a 2015 forum post; it is the vendor's own and the only one published, and the last changelog entry read is from 2016. Its table lists High-Way under 'server IPs at registration (reported)' and gives the verdict fails-egress, and its own prose then says High-Way 'gates the registration instead of the download' - which is the refusal of a class at signup, not a download-time class rule. The headline claim 'the other six refuse the class' counts High-Way as one of the six. Its own documentation refuses nothing; the gate is manual vetting, which is an identity constraint. The records that already existed each priced one line of this page and neither normalised TB to TiB, so the EUR 12.00 30-day rate and the EUR 32.50 no-expiry rate were both being compared against per-TiB figures from other lanes and each was 10% better than it is. This record carries the whole grid and the TiB normalisation. The floor is the annual 9 TB package, not the 30-day 1 TB one: EUR 8.33 per TB-month against EUR 12.00 is a 31% cut for a 12-month commitment, and the 12 TB annual (EUR 110) is worse per byte than the 9 TB annual (EUR 75), which is the one non-monotonic rung in the ladder. The 'ab' prices are floors, not prices: EUR 3.99 buys the smallest Premium package and the tariff actually needed is the byte package. The best price per TB and the only one whose currency does not rot, at the cost of a reviewed registration and a German-only contract. Fetched files are still not stored. The cheapest-looking number on the page is the wrong one: EUR 3.99 buys the plan, not traffic, and every downloaded byte is charged again through a package. At 1 TiB/month the effective price is EUR 16-32.50 per TB, which is the highest per-byte price and the reason it is not the cheapest monthly option despite the lowest headline. Free MB can be bought, so the 'free' tier is a credit scheme, not an allowance. Ranked here on mechanism rather than numbers: the factor system is real and documented, but nothing about the caps is observable without an approved account.
